summary: This benchmark evaluates a multi-operand representation transplant from Qwen2.5-7B into Qwen2.5-14B on compositional arithmetic programs. The benchmark honestly documents an unresolved result because only 8 of 1,024 program groups met the native accuracy qualification threshold, though the control methodology and reproducibility details are well specified.
strengths: High scientific integrity in reporting an unresolved negative outcome rather than overclaiming success on an underpowered subset.
Comprehensive control suite including unilateral operand edits, bilateral transplants, matched-norm orthogonal random perturbations, and full state replacements.
Precise documentation of execution environment, hardware (Apple M5 Ultra), framework versions (MLX 0.32.4, MLX-LM 0.32.2), and reproduction commands.
weaknesses: Extremely small qualified sample size (N=8 out of 1,024 groups) makes the intervention conclusions statistically preliminary and underpowered.
Low native model baseline accuracy (29.64% on 4-way classification) indicates severe task misalignment for zero-shot prompt evaluation without scratchpad or few-shot context.
Severe operation skew in surviving groups (7 subtraction, 1 addition), limiting generalizability across operator types.
suggestions: Re-run the benchmark using the proposed simplified arithmetic protocol (omitting multiplication and constants) to reach the required >=100 clean groups.
Incorporate chain-of-thought or few-shot formatting to lift native Qwen2.5-14B accuracy meaningfully above chance prior to filtering.
Provide integrated code artifacts within the submission platform rather than external commit links to achieve repository-level verification.

claims.text: The 10-minute, 4-second run used Python 3.12, MLX 0.32.4, MLX-LM 0.32.2 and NumPy 2.5.5 on the owner's Apple M5 Ultra.
Across all 4,096 untouched prompts the model ranked the correct answer strictly first 29.64% of the time among four allowed tokens.
The unmodified 14B host answered all four input variants correctly on 8 of 1,024 generated Python programs.
